purpose: Ideas that are good but do not fit the 15 September warm-up deadline. Parked here so they are not lost and not built. Each entry states why it was deferred and what would have to be true to revive it.
rule: Nothing in this file gets built before the warm-up entry ships. If one of these starts to feel urgent mid-build, that is the scope-creep signal, not a new priority.

extensions.title: ATProto lexicon for provenance-carrying run records
extensions.idea: A record schema on the AT Protocol for runs, where the route carries its provenance with it — self-owned data on a public, portable running platform rather than a closed silo.
extensions.why_it_is_good: It is the correct long-form answer to the same question GPX extensions answer cheaply: where should a provenance-carrying record actually live? Portable identity plus portable data is the structurally right home for it.
extensions.why_deferred: Designing a record schema for a protocol requires reading the current Lexicon specification properly rather than working from memory. That is a research task, not a build task, and eleven days of it would come directly out of the provenance layer, which is the part that matters for this entry.
extensions.cheap_version_shipping_now: Per-point provenance written into the GPX <extensions> block. Importers ignore what they do not understand; a text editor reveals everything.
revive_when: there is a reason to want records outside a single page
there is time to read the Lexicon spec rather than approximate it
extensions.first_step_when_revived: Read the current Lexicon spec. Then write one record type by hand and see whether the provenance model survives contact with it.

extensions.title: Strava OAuth integration
extensions.why_deferred: An OAuth application with a review process and usage terms that need reading carefully. Days of work, and nobody judging the entry will log in.
extensions.cheap_version_shipping_now: GPX download. Opens in Strava, Garmin, Komoot and Apple Fitness with no account, no key and no terms review.
revive_when: there are real users who want their runs synced, not judges who want to look at a page

extensions.title: Google Maps rendering and directions
extensions.why_deferred: Requires a billable API key, which cannot sit in a public static page without someone else spending the money.
extensions.cheap_version_shipping_now: The existing map layer and the routing already in the repo.
revive_when: never, for a public static artifact

extensions.title: Live weather in the run planner
extensions.why_deferred: Adds an external dependency in order to tell the runner something they can see out the window. Wind and inversion effects on pollution dispersion would be a real contribution, but that is a modelling project, not a display field.
revive_when: the question becomes why the readings differ, not what they are
extensions.note: There is apparently an existing weather build with connectors already set up. Worth locating before rebuilding anything here.

extensions.title: Splits, training plans, accounts, history
extensions.why_deferred: Every running app already has these. Building them makes the entry indistinguishable from a weekend project, and consumes exactly the time the differentiator needs.
revive_when: this stops being a demonstration and becomes a product someone asked for

extensions.title: Optimal circuit generation with a distance target
extensions.why_deferred: A genuinely harder problem than shortest path, and the single item most likely to consume the entire build window.
extensions.cheap_version_shipping_now: Waypoints at radius, route between them, score and return the best three. Labelled as candidates rather than an optimum.
revive_when: the three-candidate version demonstrably produces bad loops

extensions.title: Combining all five challenge datasets
extensions.why_deferred: The five share no join key beyond being Basel. The result would be five panels side by side, which is a dashboard, which is the most common and least memorable thing at any hackathon.
revive_when: never in this form; individual pairings with a real key are a different question

extensions.title: Rebuild graph construction on city2graph
extensions.why_deferred: Already evaluated twice and documented in docs/CITY2GRAPH.md. It reproduces the structural relations exactly, but sets the project's Python floor to 3.12 against a 3.9 repo, replaces about 60 lines of verified shapely, and returns a vocabulary that discards the domain semantics and provenance the project exists to demonstrate.
revive_when: proximity layers needed as first-class relations
a Python upgrade already paid for by other reasons

extensions.title: Basel Evidence — parliamentary Vorstösse joined to city data
extensions.why_deferred: A six-phase pipeline with a daily cron, an LLM extraction layer and a publication site, against a brief that says an evening is enough. It also touches none of the five challenge datasets, and publishing auto-generated evidence attached to a named politician's motion within thirteen days is where one wrong number costs more credibility than the entry earns.
revive_when: October — the main Hack am Rhein event, where the scope actually fits
